ordered_diagnoses: Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3

finalists.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
finalists.why: It has the most specific for evidence, including tongue atrophy and large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles.

finalists.label: Frontotemporal dementia
finalists.why: It has the most comprehensive for evidence, including 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, and tongue atrophy, with no against evidence.

finalists.label: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration
finalists.why: It has specific for evidence, including cognitive impairment and heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene, although it lacks some findings like vertical gaze palsy.

frontier_selector.why: The champion is chosen because it specifically accounts for the tongue atrophy and large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential, which are decisive findings in the vignette.
